objectives.text: explain the concept of economic wealth;
compare natural, human, and manufactured resources;
identify the key economic resources of Bangladesh;
define and describe different types of goods;
differentiate between non-renewable goods and economic goods;
compare durable and non-durable consumer goods;
distinguish between intermediate goods and capital goods;
explain the idea of opportunity cost and the principle of choice;
understand the interrelationship between income, savings, and investment; and compile a sector-wise list of various economic activities in Bangladesh.
Explain the concept of utility;
Understand the relationship among utility, consumption, and the consumer;
Demonstrate that total utility is the sum of marginal utilities; Illustrate the law of diminishing marginal utility using diagrams;
Analyze the relationship between price and quantity demanded; Examine the relationship between price and quantity supplied; and
Identify how equilibrium price and quantity are determined.
describe the concept of production;
explain the relationship between the producer and production;
explain the materials of production;
explain the organization and its development;
explain the relationship between average and marginal product;
explain the concept of production cost;
Identify visible and invisible costs;
Distinguish between private and social costs;
Be interested in productive activities and initiatives;
Be able to present the law of diminishing marginal product with the help of tables and graphs.
Define the concept of a market;
Describe the patterns and types of market development;
Explain the features of a perfectly competitive market;
Compare perfect competition with monopolistic and monopolistic competitive
Identify the different types of market systems in Bangladesh;
Understand the reasons behind price fluctuations and their impact;
Create a chart categorizing market types based on competition.
eo illustrate the ideas of national income;
demonstrate the differences between the national income (NI) and the gross domestic product (GDP);
compare the national income (NI) and the net national product (NNP); illustrate various methods asuring the national income;
classify the determinants of GDP in two groups, which are factors and technology; prepare a list of factors excluded from GDP;
describe the system to measure the national income in Bangladesh.
describe the idea and classification of money;
explain the functions of money;
describe the concept of a commercial bank and its main functions; illustrate the procedures of opening and operating a bank account;
explain the concept of the central bank and its major functions;
compare the central bank with commercial banks; cvaluate the role of some important banks of Bangladesh in agricultural development, industrialization and self-employment and
show the banking system of Bangladesh by drawing charts.
explain the main characteristics of Bangladeshi economy;
explain the main sectors (agriculture, industry and service) of Bangladeshi economy;
analyse the comparative importance of the main sectors (agriculture, industry and service) of Bangladeshi economy;
identify the dependence of agriculture and manufacturing sectors on one another;
discuss sectorwise analysis of the data of the economy and use it mathematically and
discuss the importance of various sectors through drawing graphs.
explain the relationship between economic growth and development;
explain the characteristics of developed, less developed and developing countries;
identify the stages of development of Bangladesh economy;
make a list of obstacles to economic development of Bangladesh;
explain the importance of development projects run by Bangladesh government;
explain the importance of development projects run by Non- Government Organisations (NGOs) for national development;
explain the type, reasons and ways of reducing poverty in Bangladesh;
analyse the nature of unemployment in Bangladesh and the ways to remove it;
explain the concept of human resources and
explain the way in which the population of a nation can become its asset.
explain what public finance is;
explain what the sources of government revenue are;
explain what the sectors of government expenditure are;
explain the concept of budget;
differentiate between current budget and capital budget;
compare between balanced budget and unbalanced budget;
explain the budget of Bangladesh government and its classifications;
identify the sources to finance the development budget of Bangladesh government and participate in the discussion of the national budget.
